Data notes for this edition
  • A clean scan. The collector finished at 07:43 ET Tuesday and every symbol ends on Monday's completed bar on every frame; no pre-market stub was found and nothing was patched.
  • The weekly column is one session old. The Oct 5–9 bar holds Monday alone, so weekly highs, lows and RSI are running figures and weekly badge changes are provisional: IONQ's weekly cell turned down from mixed on one session and may turn back. Weekly extensions and histograms are not quoted in the cards this edition.
  • Day-over-day changes are one session. The prior scan is Monday morning's, which held Friday's close, so every change chip, the breadth tile and the census describe Monday's session alone.
  • Weekday names mean this week and last. "Monday" in a card is Oct 5; "Friday" is Oct 2 and "Thursday" Oct 1. Today's session is called "today" or "the open".
  • Volume was light. Five of 24 traded at or above their 20-day average on a median 0.74×: SPCX 1.44×, MSFT 1.25×, NVDA 1.16×, AMZN 1.12× and TSLA 1.11×; ORCL's 0.50× was the lightest. 15-minute volume figures are not used.
  • Twelve cards are rewritten and seven are light-touch edits. Rewritten because a Trigger or Invalidation fired on the close, a stance changed or the row moved four notches: NVDA, MSFT, SKHY, SNDK, HOOD, META, INTC, SPCX, TSLA, IONQ, GOOGL and ORCL. AMD, MRVL, MU, PLTR, AAPL, CRWV and AMZN keep their thesis and caption with the Bias, the hold zones and the day-trade block re-pointed to Monday's averages.
  • Firsts and records, checked against the bars: QQQ 756.20, XLK 200.93 and NVDA 238.90 are the highest closes in the loaded history, and QQQ 756.92 and NVDA 240.10 the highest prints; MSFT's 525.18 is the highest close since Oct 30 2025; SPCX's since Jun 18; META's since Sep 25; TSLA's is the first close above its daily EMA200 since Sep 23; GOOGL's the first above its EMA50 since Sep 22; INTC's the first under its EMA10 since Sep 15; ORCL's a second above its EMA10.
  • Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ by cents. MSFT's last hourly close reads 525.50 against a 525.18 daily close and TSLA's 378.84 against 378.73; the daily figures are the ones the cards use for closes and ranges.
  • The daily screenshots show price and volume from the layout; every EMA, RSI, MACD and extension figure in a caption is computed from the scan, not read off the image. The images carry the platform's pre-market quote label; no figure in this report comes from it.
  • Thin histories: SKHY (61 daily bars; no EMA200, no weekly badge), SPCX (79 daily bars; no daily EMA200, no weekly badge), CRWV (no weekly EMA200).
  • The scorecard grades Monday's eight calls against Monday's hourly and daily bars. A target that prints inside the entry hour before that hour closes does not count for the entry; a gap over the reclaim with the first target under the open is not triggered; the eleven cards that were not calls are not graded.

Bottom line

  • Three record closes on a quiet tape: QQQ 756.20, XLK 200.93 and NVDA 238.90 closed at loaded-history highs on a 14 up / 10 down day, a 0.74× median volume and 18 first-hour lows.
  • The laggards did the work: TSLA +2.2% closed over its 200-day for the first time since Sep 23, GOOGL over its 50-day since Sep 22, META +1.9% out of its 725–728 cluster.
  • Chips paused, Intel broke: AMD, MRVL and the memory names held their lines on small down days; INTC −2.6% closed under 117.43 and under its 10-day for the first time since Sep 15.
  • SPCX ran again: +7.6% on 1.44×, the board's heaviest volume and best day for a second session; its 1H is +4.02 ATR, the most stretched cell on the board, so the pullback is the entry.
  • One of eight calls worked: NVDA printed both targets from a held first hour; MSFT was a partial and SKHY and SNDK washes; AMD, MRVL, MU and HOOD never reached their reclaims or their lines.

Scorecard: Monday's calls against Monday's bar (1 worked, 1 partial, 2 wash, 4 not triggered)

The opens landed on the zones this time, and most of the reclaims never held. NVDA opened over its reclaim and under its first target, held above the zone through the first hour and ran to both targets by the last hour. MSFT opened over its reclaim too, but its two near targets printed inside the entry hour and the entry at the first-hour close gave back to 525.18 after 529.01 printed. AMD, MRVL and MU each tested their deeper zone in the first hour and then failed to hold an hourly close over the reclaim; MU's first hour also undercut 1057.57 by two dollars before the daily close held it. SKHY reclaimed 195.53 at 12:30 and stalled 51 cents short of 196.48. SNDK's short printed its 14:30 close under 1698.17 by 34 cents and the last half hour took it back. HOOD never lost 112.44 and closed a nickel under the 114.16 a long needs.

Full read: a second session that held the gap and rotated into the laggards

Monday held Friday's gap and bought the first-hour dips. SPY closed 774.83, +0.7% on 0.97×, at 74% of a 769.63–776.61 range, a second close above the 766.43 EMA21 and 0.6% under its 779.37 record. QQQ closed 756.20, +0.9%, a record close after a 756.92 record print in the 14:30 hour; XLK closed 200.93, +0.6%, also a record close; SMH closed 633.90, +0.5%, 5.7% under its June high. Fourteen of 24 rose and ten fell, an average of +0.5%. The largest moves were SPCX +7.6%, TSLA +2.2%, NVDA +2.1%, META +1.9% and MSFT +1.5% against INTC −2.6%, CRWV −2.5%, IONQ −1.8%, MU −1.0% and SNDK −0.9%.

The board firmed in the middle and the down cells thinned. Up cells held at 74, down cells fell from 14 to 9 and mixed rose to 35. The daily has 17 up from 15 and one down from two; the 4H has 15 up from 17 and no down cell from one; the 1H has 16 up from 15; the 15m has 10 up from 11 and three down from seven. Six rows are up on all five timeframes, from five: SPY, IGV and NVDA joined, MSFT and AMD slipped a 15m cell. Twenty-two of 24 close above the daily EMA21 (AMZN and ORCL under) and 21 above the EMA50; fifteen carry a positive daily histogram, from thirteen.

Where the risk sits. Six daily cells are stretched, from three: SPCX +2.77, SMH +2.66, XLK +2.58, QQQ +2.44, AMD +2.24 and NVDA +2.18, with MSFT and META at +1.72. SPCX's 1H at +4.02 (RSI 77.8) and 4H at +3.59 are the most extended cells on the board, ahead of SMH's 4H at +3.07. On the other side, six names closed in the bottom third of their range after a first-hour high: MRVL, INTC, AAPL, AMZN, ORCL and CRWV. The deepest fast cells are AMZN's 15m at −1.56, ORCL's 15m at −1.43 and INTC's 1H at −1.44.

What the session says about today. Monday's lows are the new lines and most sit a percent or two under the close: NVDA 235.15, META 727.12, TSLA 364.91, MSFT 521.47, AMD 619.99 and MRVL 267.80. The names that broke are the names to watch for a second day: INTC under 117.43 with 116.00 and 113.97 the map, CRWV back under its 50-day, IONQ under 43.15. The stretched cells (SPCX, SMH, XLK, QQQ) are bought on pullbacks into the hourly averages or not at all, and the FOMC minutes on Wednesday are the next scheduled gap.

Nothing scheduled moves the board before Wednesday's Fed minutes. Tuesday carries only the trade balance at 08:30 and two low-impact Fed speakers, Bowman at 10:45 and Schmid at 13:15. Day-trading playbook

Tuesday's trade is the second day of the reclaims: NVDA is bought on a hold of 237.99–237.09 under its record, META on 741.01–739.90 over its old cluster, TSLA on 378.61–376.31 at its 200-day, MSFT on 523.73–522.45 and GOOGL on 345.38–344.48; SPCX is bought only on the pullback into 169.08–167.58; INTC is sold under 116.00 and HOOD under 112.60.

Session framing

Monday opened on Friday's closes, printed the low of the day in the first hour in 18 of 24 names and bought it: eleven closed in the top third of their range and only six in the bottom third. The buying went to the names that had lagged, TSLA, GOOGL and META, and to SPCX for a second day; the chips that had gapped on Friday rested, with AMD, MRVL and the memory names down less than a percent and holding their lines. The breaks were on the other side of the board: INTC lost 117.43 and its 10-day, IONQ lost 43.15, and CRWV closed back under its 50-day.

Five questions govern the session. Do the records get a second day: NVDA above 237.09 and QQQ above 749.94 through the first hour keep them, and 235.07 and 744.56 are the closes that end them. Do the reclaims hold: TSLA above 376.31 with the 200-day at 378.61, GOOGL above 344.48 with the 50-day at 345.35, META above 739.90. Does SPCX pull back into 169.08–167.58 and hold, or run from the open again, which is not an entry. Do the breaks continue: INTC under 116.00 targets 113.97, IONQ under 42.24 targets 42.01. And does HOOD lose 112.60 or close above 114.96.

Methodology and data notes

Pipeline, rubric, data caveats and sources

Pipeline: TradingView Desktop (CDP) → dedicated "B List Research" layout → up to 500 bars per timeframe per symbol (W / D / 240 / 60 / 15, regular sessions) → indicators computed locally: EMA 10/21/50/200, RSI-14 (Wilder), MACD 12/26/9, ATR-14 (Wilder), 20-bar relative volume, fractal (2-2) swing pivots, 252-day high/low distances, relative strength vs SPY as return differentials. Trend matrix rubric per cell, ±1 for each of six inputs: close vs EMA21, close vs EMA50, EMA21/EMA50 stack, EMA50 five-bar slope, RSI zone (≥55 = +1, ≤45 = −1, else 0) and MACD histogram sign — score ≥+4 Up, ≤−4 Down, else Chop; cells lacking an EMA21 or EMA50 return "—".

Data caveats. Captured Tuesday Oct 6 2026 at 07:43 ET, before the open; no errors were reported across the 24 symbols and every symbol ends on Monday Oct 5's completed session on every frame. No pre-market stub was found and nothing was patched. The weekly column is the running Oct 5–9 bar with one session in it; its badges, RSI and histograms move with every daily close and any weekly badge change this edition is provisional (CRWV and IONQ changed on Monday's bar alone). The prior scan for every day-over-day comparison (change chips, breadth tile, census) is Monday Oct 5's morning scan, which held Friday Oct 2's completed session, so every delta on this page is exactly one session, Monday's. Twelve cards are rewritten for this edition (NVDA, MSFT, SKHY, SNDK, HOOD, META, INTC, SPCX, TSLA, IONQ, GOOGL, ORCL). Seven (AMD, MRVL, MU, PLTR, AAPL, CRWV, AMZN) keep the thesis paragraphs and caption written on Friday's bar and carry a new Bias, day-trade block and, where the fast averages moved, re-pointed Trigger, Invalidation and ladder; their "Full read" describes Friday's session and says so. "Monday" in the cards is Oct 5, "Friday" is Oct 2 and "Thursday" is Oct 1. The 15m column is Monday's 15:45 ET bar. The final 15m bars carry the usual closing-auction volume spike and those RVOL figures were not used anywhere in this report; 15-minute readings quoted are RSI, extension and EMA position only. The same applies to 1H and 4H relative volume. All relative-volume figures in this report are daily. Hourly bars and the daily bar can differ by cents at the open and the close (auction prints); closes and ranges are quoted from the daily bar and intraday paths from the hourly bars. Fractal pivot lag. Swing pivots require two bars on each side to confirm, so a level set within the last two bars will not yet appear in the pivot sequence. Friday's and Monday's highs and lows for every name are quoted from the bars, not the pivot lists. The daily screenshots inlined in the cards and the market frame show price and volume from the layout; every EMA, RSI, MACD and extension figure quoted in a caption is computed from the scan, not read off the image. Thin histories: SKHY and SPCX have no weekly badge and no daily EMA200; CRWV has no weekly EMA200.

Scorecard. Monday's eight flagged calls, written on Friday's close, are graded against Monday's hourly and daily bars: the hourly bars decide "held an hour", the daily close decides "held a session". A gap that opens over the reclaim with the first target under the open is not triggered even when the level prints; a target that prints inside the entry hour, before that hour closes, does not count for the entry; a trade that triggers, prints no target and closes against its entry with the stop untouched is a wash. The eleven cards that were not calls are not graded in this edition.
